body.statement: Can a single data-driven confidence set based on the transition-experiment and ordered-modulus handle cover \(\psi_{\delta_n}\) uniformly over local sequences approaching both hardening boundaries, with oracle-order expected length on each separated branch; or must every honest procedure pay a logarithmic length factor determined by simultaneous uncertainty in \(\kappa\), \(\rho\), and \(H\)?
body.justification: Separated-regime validity does not answer what an analyst should do when the estimated normalizer places the multiplier near a transition.
body.gap: HeilerKazak2021Irregular adapts between regular and stable laws for a fixed target, whereas this problem has two transitions, a moving target, and an intermediate marked family.
body.consumer: A resolution would permit one automatic hardening diagnostic and interval in software without user-supplied regime labels.

obligation.what_is_open: Whether a single honest confidence set can attain oracle-order expected length through both transition neighborhoods, or whether a logarithmic adaptation penalty is necessary.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen transition handle specifies neither the local parameter spaces approaching \(h_n=0\) and \(h_n=\infty\), nor a loss, coverage class, or ordered modulus.  Without those objects, both an adaptive upper construction and a least-favorable lower pair are mathematically underdetermined; separated-regime coverage alone does not select between the two alternatives in the question.
obligation.attempted: The normalizer expansion and continuity of the critical quantiles were propagated to shrinking neighborhoods.  They identify a logarithmically amplified tail-index error, but do not provide two contiguous laws with separated target values, and therefore cannot certify that the logarithm is unavoidable.  Conversely, no branch-selection rule in the frozen core controls coverage on both boundary-local experiments.
obligation.partial_result: The three explicit intervals are uniformly valid on the separated sets \(h_n\leq\eta_n\), \(h_n\in[h_-,h_+]\), and \(h_n\geq M_n\), and their scales are respectively \(\sigma_n/\sqrt n\) and \(a_n/n\).  The calibration proof also gives \(\log(\widehat a_n/a_n)=O_P((\log n)\{r_n+t_n^\rho+[nT(t_n)]^{-1/2}\})\).  These facts quantify the normalizer uncertainty that any transition procedure must accommodate, but they do not determine an ordered modulus at either moving boundary.
